462	(* Stanley EC1 §1.6, Prop. 1.6.4: for S ⊆ [n-1], define ω(S) ⊆ [n-2] by
463	   "i ∈ ω(S) iff exactly one of i, i+1 lies in S". We encode ω-maps as
464	   functions {set 'I_n.+1} → {set 'I_n} (aligning with how `beta` sees
465	   descent-sets for perms of 'I_n.+2 — the +1 shift matches Stanley's
466	   "[n-2]" vs "[n-1]"). The target β-axioms in §C use descent-sets of type
467	   {set 'I_n} (no .+1); callers bridge via the obvious `Ordinal` packaging.
468	
469	   NOTE ON THE PLAN: STANLEY_CDINDEX_PLAN.md §2 asserts that toggling any
470	   "both-in-D" descent gives a strict ω-superset. Direct case-analysis
471	   (mirrored in the proof below) shows this is TOO STRONG: toggling `i` also
472	   flips the ω-bit at `i-1`, and that bit LEAVES ω(D) precisely when
473	   (i-1) ∉ D. A concrete counterexample: D = {1,2} ⊆ 'I_3, i = 1:
474	     ω(D) = {0}, ω(toggle D 1) = ω({2}) = {1}; neither contains the other.
475	   The strict-superset statement is therefore accurate only under the extra
476	   hypothesis that `i-1 ∈ D` (Case A of the flip analysis) OR that `i = 0`
477	   (no predecessor bit to flip). We expose both the strong, correctly
478	   hypothesised bridge (`toggle_at_omega_strict_superset`) and the always-
479	   true "new bit" lemma (`toggle_at_omega_bit_i_new`). Closing the axioms
480	   of §C via the bridge will therefore require either the full Stanley
481	   cd-index nonneg theorem (M5/M6 of the plan) or a case split on
